info.title: Galaxy Explorer API
info.description: REST API for building and exploring galaxies. Bodies are JSON in camelCase, wrapped as `{ "data": … }`; lists add `nextCursor`. Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json. Every write is one change batch (X-GE-Batch-Id in the response), which can be reverted. Updates need the `version` you read. Conventions: docs/plan/architecture.md §5. Rate limits (429 with Retry-After): `default`: 600 a minute per token, account or address. Every route without a tier, sharing one budget: ten requests a second. `media`: 3000 a minute per token, account or address. Media files and the check before each (`/media-access`): a gallery is many images at once, and they don’t count against the rest. `auth`: 10 a minute per address. Signing in and changing a password: guessing. Failed tries are limited further, per address and per username (5 in 15 minutes). `links`: 20 a minute per address. Invite and reset links, and share links: guessing. `members`: 60 an hour per token, account or address. Adding a member, whose answer says whether a username exists. `uploads`: 120 an hour per token, account or address. Uploads and imports: storage and the work of reading them. A route's tier is its `x-ge-rate-limit`. LLM agents: read [the guide](/api/llm-guide.md) first; the MCP server (apps/mcp) offers these routes as tools.

get.summary: Check that the API and its database are up
get.description: Returns 200 with `status: "ok"` when the database answers, and 503 with `status: "degraded"` and `db: "down"` when it does not.

post.description: Signs in with a username, a password and, for an account with two-factor codes on, a current code (D-47), and sets the session cookie (30 days, renewed as it’s used). Any mistake gets the same 401; the right password without a needed code gets a 401 whose `errors` name `/totp`. Five failures in 15 minutes from one address, or for one username, get 429s until the window passes.
Ends this session and clears its cookie. Signed out already, it does nothing.

get.description: Whether the link is an invite or a reset, and whether it still works (`ready`), was used, or expired. An unknown link is a 404.

post.summary: Step 1 of a link: username and password
post.description: Checks the username (an invite only; 409 if it’s taken) and the password, and returns the sealed `setup` to send back to `finish`. With `twoFactor` (the default) it also returns a new two-factor secret, as text and as a QR code; with `twoFactor: false` the account will have codes off (D-47), and those are null. Nothing is saved yet.

post.summary: Step 2 of a link: the first code, if any
post.description: Checks one code from the authenticator app against the setup from `start`, if it set up two-factor codes. Then the account is made (an invite) or its password and two-factor codes are replaced and its sessions ended (a reset), the link is used up, and this browser is signed in.

Needs the current password, and a current code from the authenticator app if the account has two-factor codes on. Every other device is signed out; this one stays signed in. Failures count against the same limits as signing in.

post.summary: Run many operations as one change
post.description:
Runs up to 1000 operations in order, in one transaction and one change batch: all of them happen, or none do, and the whole request is one undo step.

Operations: create, update, delete and upsert for any entity kind (`kind` is celestial_object, group, route, place, event, character; `data` is the same body as that kind's single-resource route), and setLocation, addMembers, removeMembers, setWaypoints (a route's object ids in order), setFacts, addLink and addRelation on an entity `id`.

Refer to an entity created earlier in the same request as `"$op:N"` (N counts from 0), anywhere an id goes. For example, create a system, then planets with `"parentId": "$op:0"`.

If an operation fails, nothing is written, and the problem response's `operationIndex` names it. With `dryRun: true` everything runs and is reported, including `impact` (rows touched per table), and then rolled back; use it to preview deletes.

post.summary: Import an export’s zip, or a CSV of objects
post.description:
Send `multipart/form-data` with one file in a field named `file`: an export's zip, or a CSV of objects with the columns name, base_type, x, y, z, parent_key, group_key, external_key (a CSV needs `mapId`). At most 200 MB.

`mode=create` adds everything as new entries; a key already used, or the slug of a map that has entries, is a conflict (an empty map with the slug is filled, as a new universe's first map is). `mode=merge` updates entries by their externalKey and adds the rest, leaving out entries without a key. Settings rows, assets and maps are matched by name, hash and slug in both modes. For an entry a merge updates, each aspect the file lists (facts, images, links…) replaces the entry's; an aspect the file leaves out stays.

`dryRun=true` does everything, reports it and rolls back: use it first. A real import is one change batch (one undo). If the report has conflicts or unresolved references, nothing is written and the answer is 409 with `report`.

tags.description: Who can see a universe: its members (editors and viewers), its share link, and handing it to another account (M8-T12).

tags.name: objects
tags.description: A celestial object: a system, star, planet, moon, asteroid belt, station, nebula, anomaly, black hole or marker (`baseType`). Objects nest: `parentId` is the object it sits inside, or null for the top level of the galaxy. Which parents a base type allows is fixed (a planet goes in a system or the galaxy; a moon in a planet). x, y, z are a position in the parent's frame: light-years in the galaxy (+Y is galactic north), system units (roughly AU) inside a system, and body radii around a planet. `explorable` makes systems open a system view and planets or moons an orbit view. `appearance` holds only overrides of the type and subtype defaults.

tags.name: groups
tags.description: A named set of top-level objects drawn as a colored outline: a sector, territory or faction. Its `groupTypeId` (a universe setting) decides which layer it belongs to and how groups nest: a Sub-sector's `parentGroupId` must be a Sector. An object is in at most one group of each type. Members are managed under /groups/{id}/members. `outlineColor` defaults to the group type's color.

tags.name: routes
tags.description: A line through objects in order: a trade lane, warp route or campaign path (U6). Its waypoints, the objects it passes through, are set as an ordered list of object ids with PUT /routes/{id}/waypoints (or the batch op setWaypoints); they are top-level objects on the route's map, and one may come again later (a round trip) but not twice in a row. `style` holds the line color, width in pixels and dashing.

tags.name: places
tags.description: A lasting place, such as a city, fortress or ruin. Where it is lives in its location (PUT /entities/{id}/location): on a planet or moon at a latitude and longitude, at an object, at a position in space, or at another place.

tags.name: events
tags.description: Something that happened. `dateText` is free text in the universe's own date format (such as "240.M41"); `dateSort` is an optional number to order events by. It may have a location like a place, and characters relate to it with the `participant` relation.

tags.name: characters
tags.description: A person or being, shared by every map of the universe (characters belong to the universe, not to one map). Link a character to the events they took part in with the `participant` relation.

tags.name: group-types
tags.description: A kind of group in this universe, such as Segmentum, Sector or Sub-sector (T5). `layer` gathers types shown together (Administrative, Political). `parentGroupTypeId` makes types nest: groups of this type sit inside groups of the parent type.

tags.name: event-categories
tags.description: A category for events, with the icon and color of their pins, such as Battle or Discovery.

tags.name: object-subtypes
tags.description: A universe-specific refinement of an object base type, such as Hive World (a planet) or Webway Gate (an anomaly) (U2). `defaultAppearance` sits between the base type's defaults and each object's overrides.

tags.name: field-definitions
tags.description: A custom fact this universe records, such as Population or Tithe Grade (U2). Entities get values for it under /entities/{id}/facts. `valueType` is text, number, date_text or url. `appliesToKind` (and optionally a base type or subtype) says which entities it is for.

tags.name: images
tags.description: Uploaded images attached to an entity.

tags.name: assets
tags.description: Uploading images, and the universe’s image library.

tags.name: icons
tags.description: The bundled icon sets for event categories and pins: Lucide and game-icons.net (M6-T4).

tags.name: site
tags.description: The public site’s own pages (M8-T9): what the attributions page lists, and the pages link-preview fetchers get.
